newsitem.title: USA: Roche to acquire Tastemaker flavorings.
newsitem.headline: Roche to acquire Tastemaker flavorings.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals concern Roche Holding AG has agreed to acquire the worldwide businesses and operations of U.S.-based Tastemaker, a maker of food flavorings, the companies said Wednesday.
The companies did not disclose the purchase price.
Roche said the deal is part of its goal to strengthen its four core businesses -- pharmaceuticals, vitamins and fine chemicals, diagnostics, and fragrances and flavors.
Tastemaker will "be an excellent strategic fit and will ideally complement the activities of Givaudan-Roure, Roche's fragrances and flavors division," Roche said.
Givaudan-Roure is an international company in the fragrances, flavors and aroma chemicals business. It had consolidated sales of 1.4 billion Swiss francs ($981 million) in 1996.

Tastemaker, a 50-50 partnership between Hercules Inc. and Mallinckrodt Inc., makes flavoring and citrus specialities used in foods and beverages. The Cincinnati-based company has about 1,280 employees in the United States, Holland, England, Mexico, Australia and Japan, and had 1996 sales of about $320 million.
Roche is a worldwide research-based health care group with some 50,000 employees in more than 100 countries. It recorded 1996 sales of about 16 billion Swiss francs ($11.2 billion).
News of Roche's acquisition disappointed some market participants who had expected Roche to spin off the whole division, traders said.
